relight.fullCoverage.why: rule, stated before measuring (highlight fix, 2026-11-14): the highlight law's brightest-1% condition reads only pixels whose sheet coverage is at least this. On a shape's edge the only coverage between 0 and 1 is the field's anti-alias ramp (bar 06 and test/pages/islands.html: 1 - smoothstep(-aa, aa, d), one texel either side of the edge). A ramp texel within half an 8-bit level of 1 (1 - 0.5 / 255 = 0.99804) is stored as full on the 8-bit sheet, so the float sheet counts the same texels as full and the law reads the same pixels on either format; half a level rounded down to the third decimal is 0.002, so 1 - 0.002. Such a texel mixes at most 0.2% of the ground into its colour. Set from the sheet's storage, not from any page's reading (review-bar-06, Critical 1).

relight.falloffSpan.why: Rule, stated before its value (Phase 2 Task 3, per page): the falloff fit resolves the exponent only when its samples span ln(dmax / dmin) of at least this value x the page's own fit rms. The page's own rms is that of its widest fit (the cone opened so the outer samples sit 45 degrees off the aim; the declared cone's when it is already that wide), because a narrow fit's own rms proved not to be a safe noise measure. On its own rms that declared cone would resolve at seed 2 (0.0217 >= 4 x 0.0052 = 0.0208) and its exponent 1.06 would pass the slack; its widest fit's rms (0.0245) opens it. flash.maxPerSecond.why: by definition, from WCAG 2.3.1: content passes with 'no more than three general flashes and / or no more than three red flashes within any one-second period' (WCAG 2.2 (and 2.1) definition, 'general flash and red flash thresholds'). A flash is two opposing transitions, so a span fails at 7 or more counted transitions (3.5 flashes).

flash.areaShare.why: by definition, with paint-kit's reading of 'concurrently': content also passes when 'the combined area of flashes occurring concurrently and contiguously' is no more than .006 sr, '25% of any 10 degree visual field' (WCAG 2.2 (and 2.1) definition, 'general flash and red flash thresholds'; Understanding 2.3.1). A window fails a span when the samples that flash more than flash.maxPerSecond times in that 1 s span cover more than this share of 341 x 256 CSS px. This reading is paint-kit's, not a quote, and stricter than the text in two named ways: a sample counts whatever its phase (not only when lit on the same frame), and the flashing samples need not be contiguous. Both can only fail a page the text might pass.

flash.windowWidth.why: by definition: Note 1 of the WCAG 2.2 (and 2.1) definition, 'general flash and red flash thresholds': a 341 x 256 px rectangle at 1024 x 768 estimates a 10 degree visual field; the Understanding page for 2.3.1 substitutes CSS px for those pixels (87,296 CSS px).

flash.windowHeight.why: by definition: the height of the 341 x 256 CSS px 10 degree field (flash.windowWidth).

flash.lumaDelta.why: by definition: a general flash is 'a pair of opposing changes in relative luminance of 10% or more of the maximum relative luminance (1.0)' (WCAG 2.2 (and 2.1) definition, 'general flash and red flash thresholds'). Also the size below which a reversal does not end a transition (a smaller swing cannot be a transition), so pixel noise cannot split one change into two.

flash.darkMax.why: by definition: a general flash counts only 'where the relative luminance of the darker image is below 0.80' (WCAG 2.2 (and 2.1) definition, 'general flash and red flash thresholds').

flash.redRatio.why: by definition: Note 3 of the WCAG 2.2 (and 2.1) definition, 'general flash and red flash thresholds': one transition of a red flash is to or from a state with R/(R+G+B) >= 0.8. R, G, B are taken linear (decoded as for relative luminance), as WCAG 2.0's red definition said; Note 3 does not say.

flash.redChroma.why: by definition: Note 3 of the WCAG 2.2 (and 2.1) definition, 'general flash and red flash thresholds': the difference between the two states of a red transition is more than 0.2 in the CIE 1976 UCS (u'v') chromaticity diagram. Measured here as the u'v' distance from the sample's first saturated red state (the states before it are known by their u'v range, so the leg into it is measured from that range's farthest corner).

flash.cell.why: a measuring step, not a pass mark: the side in CSS px of the box each sample averages (its mean linear sRGB). WCAG exempts a fine balanced pattern with squares under 0.1 degree; with 341 CSS px as 10 degrees, 0.1 degree is 3.41 CSS px. A 4 px box averages any pattern that repeats every 4, 2 or 1 px (a 1 px or 2 px checkerboard, 1 px or 2 px stripes) to its exact mean at any offset, so those exempt patterns read as still. It does not average away a pattern of 4 px squares or larger: some boxes keep its full swing, and the one-sample lines where it balances are filled by the area's closing (flash-count.ts). It does not fully remove 3 px squares (exempt) or pixel noise, so those can count: stricter than the text, never looser. A 3 px box, the review's proposal, leaves a 2 px black / white checkerboard a 1/9 swing (0.111, over flash.lumaDelta), so it would fail an exempt pattern.

flash.stride.why: a measuring step, not a pass mark: the distance in CSS px between samples (boxes of flash.cell px), so boxes overlap by half. Half the box is the largest step at which a pattern of 4 px squares at any offset keeps a full-swing sample every 4 px, so the closing (one sample) joins them into the whole patch; a step of a whole box lets a 4 px checkerboard balance in every box at a 2 px offset. Each sample stands for stride x stride px of area; it is also the window stride. Cost: 479 x 299 samples on a 960 x 600 frame, a fixed tracker state of about 70 bytes per sample, no frames kept.

flash.tailSeconds.why: a measuring span, not a pass mark: the check steps a page from t 0 to its settle time (bar.json, 0 when unset) plus this many seconds, at the engine's 60 ticks per s, so every 1 s span of the intro and two spans of what follows are counted. A bar with a longer flashing loop overrides it in bar.json.
